slides.title: Background
slides.content: In summer 1956, a group of researchers gathered at Dartmouth College to explore the idea that aspects of learning and intelligence could be precisely described and simulated by machines.
bullets: Location: Dartmouth College, Hanover, New Hampshire

slides.title: Key Organizers & Participants
slides.content: The proposal and workshop brought together pioneers of computing and cognition.
bullets: Other attendees included Allen Newell and Herbert A. Simon

slides.title: Core Ideas Proposed
slides.content: The proposal suggested that machines could be made to simulate human intelligence.

slides.title: Impact & Legacy
slides.content: The Dartmouth workshop helped establish AI as a field and shaped decades of research.
bullets: Set an ambitious agenda for symbolic AI
Influenced research directions, optimism, and later AI winters
Remembered as a foundational moment in computing history

slides.title: Key Takeaway
slides.content: A small summer workshop launched a field that continues to transform science, business, and society.
